newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks rise in bourse trade, U.S supports.
newsitem.headline: German stocks rise in bourse trade, U.S supports.

text.p: German shares climbed in bourse trade on Monday, encouraged by Friday's strength on Wall Street. Although trade was light, dealers said they saw demand rising and the DAX index testing the important 2,700 level.
The DAX index of 30 blue-chip stocks was 8.83 points, or 0.33 percent, firmer at 2,694.86.
"The market is holding itself well at these higher levels," said one trader. "The 2,700 level will be tested again this week."
Early last week the DAX index reached record highs above the psychological and technical level of 2,700, but then fell back somewhat and traders said the market was consolidating at the new highs.
The dollar held just above the crucial 1.53 mark level, which was supportive for export-oriented German stocks.

On Monday the chemicals sector was a favourite, dealers said, leading the market higher with Bayer AG up 45 pfennigs at 58.30, BASF AG up 62 pfennigs at 49.70 and Hoechst AG gaining 65 pfennigs to stand at 58.40.
Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, in the spotlight since last week on talk that Deutsche Bank AG has upped its ownership in the Bavarian bank, was up 58 pfennigs at 55.80.

Amongst the medium-sized firms engineering company Deutsche Babcock AG dropped over ten percent, falling 5.70 marks to 46.20 after it said it would incur a higher charge for its restructuring measures than originally expected.
New stock Fresenius Medical Care continued to attract interest, gaining almost five percent in early bourse trade, rising 6.60 marks to 123.40, after the stock rose in the U.S.
Pharmaceuticals firm Gehe AG climbed 2.60 marks to 107.60 after it said it would sell off a generic drugs unit.

Meanwhile lead creditor Deutsche Bank of Traub AG sought the suspension of the engineering company's stock. The firm said it faced serious liqidity problems and its creditors would meet later on Monday.

U.S. consumer prices due mid-week are expected to give a clearer picture of the inflation outlook across the Atlantic and will be the main focus in what otherwise looks a fairly arid week for market-moving news, dealers said.
